newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends down slightly on Asian rains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends down slightly on Asian rains.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended slightly lower on Monday after rains fell in Thailand, improving crop prospects, traders said.

The outlook for Thai rice production for the 1997/98 season (April-March) improved with increased rainfall but the threat of insufficient rain remained in some areas, Thai government and industry sources said.

The meteorological department there said the amount of rainfall has increased substantially in the last few weeks in the central, northern and northeastern regions, Thailand's major rice producing areas.
Meanwhile, U.S. domestic and export demand was slack and traders said there were indications of increased farmer selling interest.
Rice ended 2-1/2 cents per cwt lower to unchanged with September down 2-1/2 at $9.75-1/2. Volume was estimated by CBOT at 200 lots, against Friday's actual volume of 869 lots.
